extra.message: updateContentPermission runs the ancestor owner-chain walk unconditionally whenever checkOwnership fails on the content's current owner, instead of nesting it under the ownerContentId reassignment check. A user who owns any ancestor in a content's ownership chain can therefore update content they do not own and are not reassigning, bypassing the intended ownership authorization check.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: partyGroupPermissionCheck sets altPermission='PARTYMGR_GRP' and then delegates to partyStatusPermissionCheck, which overwrites altPermission with 'PARTYMGR_STS' before invoking basePermissionCheck. The intended PARTYMGR_GRP authorization check is never performed, so a user holding only PARTYMGR_STS passes the party-group permission check.

partyRolePermissionCheck sets altPermission='PARTYMGR_ROLE' and then delegates to partyStatusPermissionCheck, which overwrites altPermission with 'PARTYMGR_STS'. The intended PARTYMGR_ROLE authorization check is discarded, so a user holding only PARTYMGR_STS passes the party-role permission check.

partyCommunicationEventPermissionCheck selects altPermission PARTYMGR_CME-EMAIL / PARTYMGR_CME-NOTE without checking that the action is CREATE. For UPDATE/DELETE requests the record-ownership check (partyIdFrom/partyIdTo/partyId versus userLogin.partyId) is skipped entirely, so a user holding the communication-event permission can modify or delete another party's EMAIL_COMMUNICATION/COMMENT_NOTE records.

checkUpdateQuoteStatus sets the quote status to QUO_ORDERED without any ORDERMGR_UPDATE permission check. Any authenticated user can mark an arbitrary quote (identified only by caller-supplied parameters) as ordered.

removeQuoteItem deletes QuoteItem records (and related QuoteTerm/QuoteAdjustment rows) without any ORDERMGR_DELETE permission check or ownership check. Any authenticated user can delete line items from an arbitrary quote by supplying its quoteId/quoteItemSeqId.

extra.message: createQuoteAdjustment creates QuoteAdjustment records (discounts/surcharges) without any ORDERMGR_CREATE permission check. Any authenticated user can fabricate adjustments on an arbitrary quote, altering pricing/amounts they are not authorized to modify.

productPriceGenericPermission assigns result.hasPermission = ServiceUtil.isSuccess(result) && checkProductRelatedPermission(...). checkProductRelatedPermission returns a Map, which is always truthy in Groovy even on a failed permission check, so the product-scoped LTD_ADMIN/alternatePermissionRoot authorization check is effectively ignored: any caller holding CATALOG_PRICE_MAINT passes regardless of the sub-check result. The subsequent fail() call also does not exist in this DSL (throws instead of returning a clean denial).
